What to understand at MT0

Military Tier (MT)
Your overall prestige stage. It determines which systems you can access. It is separate from the strength of an individual module.
Module and blueprint
A module supplies an attack, defense or utility effect. Your blueprint is the collection you equip for a tower test. Owning a module does not automatically equip it.
Module level and tier
Levels improve a module within its current tier. A tier is a larger upgrade stage. Workshop upgrades persist between ordinary tower tests; upgrades bought during a run are temporary.

What you are working toward

  • Open Headquarters and read the objectives for MT1. The supplied older reference lists 10 maximized modules and 3 regions; check the current screen before treating either as a fixed target.
  • Have a blueprint that clears the next required region reliably, and maximize the number of modules Headquarters requests.

Milestone reference; the current game takes precedence. [S02]

A practical route through this stage

The order below is an editorial synthesis of the supplied community research. It is a suggested route, not the only valid build or a tested speedrun.

  1. Build around the starting modules

    Use Basic Attack, Attack Speed, Stone Foundation and Basic Regeneration as a simple starting point. Attack determines whether enemies die before surrounding you; foundation and regeneration give you time to recover. Upgrade the Workshop through the Construction Firm when building limits stop further progress. [S03]

  2. Spend on the failure you can see

    If enemies accumulate while you stay healthy, improve damage and attack speed. If the tower loses health despite killing enemies, improve its foundation and healing. Make a few upgrades, repeat the same test, and compare the result before changing several things at once. This is a diagnostic approach rather than a required build order. [S03]

  3. Collect useful Forest rewards

    The supplied research lists Basic Bouncing at wave 10, Multishot at 30, Nature’s Touch at 40 and Wave Resources at 50. Check each reward in the module reference. Bouncing and multishot help one attack deal with more targets; Nature’s Touch combines damage with healing. Equip useful rewards and upgrade them before testing again. [S03] [S06]

  4. Use Easy clears to open the map

    Clear available Easy regions to unlock subsequent regions. Return to a reliable farming run when the next clear is too difficult. A repeatable run that funds upgrades is useful even if it does not set a record. Once combat works, spend on the additional modules needed for the promotion objective. [S03] [S02]

  5. Promote with the reset in mind

    Read the reset preview in Headquarters before confirming. Promotion changes your module levels and cube-resource economy, while unlocking new progression tools. Do not assume a military promotion behaves like simply ending a tower test. After reaching MT1, inspect workers and your first military perk. [S02] [S05]

If you are stuck

I unlocked a module but nothing changed

Check that it is equipped in the blueprint you actually started with. Then check its Workshop level.

I can clear regions but cannot promote

A region clear and a module objective are separate. Read every unfinished Headquarters objective rather than repeating a completed combat goal.

Ready to move on?

  • Every MT1 objective is complete in Headquarters.
  • You have read the reset preview and know which upgrades you will rebuild.
After the promotion

At MT1, use workers and improved production to make the next rebuild easier. Backups is a useful first-perk candidate: its protection helps on later promotions, not retroactively on the promotion you just completed. [S02] [S05]
